input: Research Boeing (boeing.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: ULA (50% owned by Boeing) is targeting November 13, 2026 for the Vulcan rocket's return to flight after a nine-month grounding. The mission is Vulcan Leo 1, carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites and flying a redesigned Northrop Grumman booster nozzle. Testing and analysis continue alongside the flight.

In its Q3 10-Q, Boeing says it expects to give ULA additional financial support in Q4 2026 and could take losses if Vulcan launches do not resume on the assumed timeline. Boeing's ULA equity investment was $572M; no support amount is disclosed.

Notices for the Commercial Airplanes job cuts (about 5%, roughly 2,500 roles, through attrition plus layoffs) start going out in December 2026. Boeing also expects to start moving the 787 from 8 to 10 per month around December 2026.

The sale of Insitu, Wisk Aero and SkyGrid to Archer Aviation, paid in roughly 19.75% of Archer's Class A stock plus warrants for up to $200M in further shares, is expected to close later in 2026 subject to regulatory approval. Held-for-sale assets were $688M at 9/30/26.

On the Q3 call, management said it would give program-level 2027 delivery detail in January. It expects 2027 Commercial deliveries to rise 10% or more and about 30 pre-built 737-7/-10s to deliver in 2027. The Q4 earnings date is not yet confirmed.
Boeing's 2.70% senior notes ($1.0B issued, CUSIP 097023CM5) mature on February 1, 2027. The amount currently outstanding is not confirmed.

777X: management still targets first delivery in 2027. The cash targets assume certification by mid-2027, and ETOPS and other flight-test authorizations are still outstanding. A slip into later 2027 could cut 2027 deliveries by about 10-15 aircraft, which management says the ~$3B 2027 FCF target can absorb.
737 MAX: stabilizing at 47 per month now runs into 2027, with wings as the pacing item. The next step to 52 per month is targeted for the second half of 2027.

The purchase price allocation for Spirit AeroSystems (closed Dec 8, 2025) is still preliminary and must be finalized within one year of close. Provisional goodwill is $10.6B, all assigned to Commercial Airplanes.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 27): revenue $24.19B (+4% YoY); GAAP EPS -$0.26; core EPS -$0.34; operating cash flow $1.50B; FCF $464M, after about $0.7B of DOJ settlement payments; total backlog a record $745.4B.

Against consensus, core EPS of -$0.34 missed the -$0.25 estimate. Revenue of $24.2B beat the $23.9B estimate, and adjusted FCF of $464M beat the $325.1M estimate (Newsquawk). TIKR used different figures: -$0.20 EPS and $24.37B revenue, which would make revenue a slight miss.

Segment results: Commercial Airplanes revenue $10.72B (-3%) at a -6.5% margin; Defense, Space & Security $7.94B (+15%) at 6.2%, which includes a $252M gain on the HRL Laboratories sale; Global Services $5.57B at 18.3%. Q3 deliveries were 161 (737: 124; 787: 22). Net cumulative catch-up adjustments cut Q3 operating earnings by $105M.

2026 FCF was narrowed to about $2B from the prior $1-3B range. Management set targets of about $3B in 2027, $6B in 2028 and $10B in 2029, with capex of about $5B in 2027 and about $4B a year in 2028-29.

Delivery guidance cut: 2026 737 deliveries will fall short of 500, and 787 deliveries will land at the low end of 90-100. Commercial Airplanes breakeven is targeted for early 2028. Abnormal costs from the 777F/767 supplier disruption will weigh on margins into the first half of 2027.

The stock fell about 10-11% on the print to roughly $168. The 52-week high is $254, and the stock is down 27% over six months. Jefferies called the FCF targets 'disappointing', saying each year's goal had slipped by about a year.

event_driven.claim: Boeing won the Navy's F/A-XX sixth-generation fighter. The full-scale development contract is worth more than $20B. The contract type was not disclosed, and Boeing excludes the award from backlog until source selection is complete.

Boeing is selling Insitu, Wisk Aero and SkyGrid to Archer Aviation for Archer stock and warrants that would give it a stake of nearly 20%. It will also invest up to $55M in an upcoming Archer funding round, keeping access to Wisk's autonomy technology through cross-licensing (deal announced Aug 10, 2026).

The Spirit AeroSystems acquisition closed Dec 8, 2025 for total consideration of $8.389B. The 10-Q also reports $1.89B of off-market customer contract liabilities that amortize into revenue through 2030.

No share buybacks were made in the nine months to 9/30/26 (the cash flow statement shows no repurchases). The CFO has put debt reduction first, then investment, with shareholder returns considered 'at the right time'.
China: on May 14, 2026, Trump said China agreed to buy 200 Boeing jets, against roughly 500 expected by some analysts. It was not confirmed as firm orders, and BA closed down 4.73% that day.

credit_signals.claim: Balance sheet at 9/30/26: $20.7B of cash and marketable securities, $45.9B of consolidated debt (flat QoQ) and $10.0B of undrawn credit facilities.

Debt repayments were $8.415B in the nine months to 9/30/26. Short-term debt fell to $4.569B from $8.461B and long-term debt to $41.351B from $45.637B. Spirit-acquired debt was $329M short-term and $3.279B long-term.
As of Dec 2025, the CFO had laid out about $8B of debt repayment in 2026 and about $4B in 2027, plus roughly $3B of Spirit debt to retire, with a $10B minimum cash benchmark.
Ratings: Fitch affirmed BBB- in June 2026 and moved the outlook to positive from stable. S&P is BBB- stable and Moody's Baa3 stable, so Boeing sits one notch above high yield at all three.
Boeing and Lockheed Martin each guarantee $750M of ULA credit facilities maturing Aug 28, 2029. This is a contingent exposure while Vulcan is grounded.

Cash quality: customer advances and progress billings rose $3.44B in Q3 and $8.1B year-to-date to $67.5B. Stripping out that build, nine-month operating cash flow would be about -$5.4B (the author's calculation, not a Boeing figure).

alternative_signals.claim: Commercial Airplanes will cut about 5% of its workforce (about 2,500 of 50,494 employees) through attrition and layoffs, with notices from December 2026. It is Boeing's first job reduction in nearly two years. BCA CEO Stephanie Pope said Boeing is 'in an overstaffed position' after slowing production schedules.
KUOW reports the Renton wing shop could not keep pace with the move from 42 to 47 per month. The IAM machinists and SPEEA unions are both seeking details on the cuts.

A dispute with Vaero, a sole-source rib-kit supplier in Jacksonville, stalled 777F wing production for weeks and also hit the 767. The CFO said shipments have resumed but a production 'gap' will flow through over the next few quarters as abnormal costs.

Avolon finalized an order for 140 737-10s on Nov 4, 2026, the largest 737 MAX order ever by a lessor. Lessors have firmly ordered more than 230 737-10s in 2026, five times the lessor 737-10 backlog at end-2025.

Contract wins: a seven-year PAC-3 seeker contract (to triple production), 22 more F-15EX (120 now under contract), $359M of additional NASA funding for Starliner and a KC-46A Lot 13 order. Commercial booked 300 net orders in Q3.
Earlier in 2026, Boeing signed a new four-year contract with SPEEA (engineers and technicians, Pacific Northwest), avoiding a strike.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Director Mortimer J. Buckley bought 5,820 shares on the open market at $171.55 on Oct 30, 2026, taking his direct holding to 10,250 shares (Form 4, code P, signed Nov 3).
Director Steven M. Mollenkopf bought 2,950 shares on the open market at a $173.03 weighted average on Oct 30, 2026, taking his direct holding to 6,717 shares (Form 4, code P).

risks.claim: The ramp keeps slipping. Stabilizing the 737 at 47 per month has moved into 2027 with wings as the bottleneck, rate 52 depends on wing and fuselage stability, and Wichita fuselage inventory is running down faster than planned.

777X certification is not done: ETOPS and other flight-test authorizations are pending. 777X work-in-process inventory rose to $7.6B from $4.3B, and 777X/767 reach-forward losses were $5.14B in the nine months to 9/30/25.
The 2027 cash bridge depends on deposits. Management flagged a 'few billion dollar' headwind from lower customer deposits and about $1B of higher capex in 2027.
Inventory recovery risk: $14.0B of 737 deferred production costs and $14.4B of 787 deferred production costs, of which $1.874B depends on future orders that are not yet firm.

ULA/Vulcan: the investigation into two nozzle failures is still open, and the Space Force has not confirmed when national security payloads can return to Vulcan. A failed return to flight would raise Boeing's support needs and loss risk.
Single-source supply chain fragility, shown by the Vaero rib-kit dispute that halted 777F wing work, with costs running through upcoming quarters.
Ratings headroom is thin at BBB-/Baa3 against $45.9B of debt. A ramp or FCF slip could stall the upgrade path implied by Fitch's positive outlook.

output.research_view: Boeing's turnaround has been pushed back by about a year. The 737 has stalled on wings, 2026 FCF is about $2B, and the $10B FCF target moved to 2029. Free cash flow now leans heavily on customer advances, and on Nov 9 Boeing announced a 5% cut to the Commercial Airplanes workforce. Against that, backlog is a record $745B, the 737-7/-10 are certified (with demand like Avolon's 140-jet order), defense is improving with the F/A-XX win, and two directors bought stock at about $172 on Oct 30. Over the next six months the stock likely depends on three things: whether the 737 holds 47 per month with 787 rate 10 by the turn of the year, a clean Vulcan return to flight (Nov 13) that limits ULA support, and whether January's 2027 detail plus 777X testing support the ~$3B 2027 FCF and mid-2027 certification assumptions.
